what_it_does: Doing math inside the memory chip itself — rather than sending data back and forth to a separate processor — can save a lot of energy, but the circuitry that converts the analog result of in-memory math back into a digital number (called an analog-to-digital converter, or ADC) normally takes up a lot of chip area and wastes power. This paper proposes a 256-by-128 memory array that shares a single set of reference voltages across many ADC circuits, and uses a clever charge-sharing accumulator to add up partial results bit by bit, reducing both the area and energy costs of conversion. The design also uses a three-level (ternary) scheme for storing model weights — each weight can be −1, 0, or +1 — and separates the read and write paths so they do not interfere with each other.
